_comment: System and Services Acquisition Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with CM (SA-10 developer CM is the upstream of CM-2 / CM-3), RA (SA-11 testing produces vuln data into RA-5 / SI-2; SA-15(3) criticality echoes RA-9), SR (SA-4 acquisition requirements are the SR vehicle for federal SCRM), and SI (SA-15 secure tooling produces the SBOM / signed artifacts SI-7 verifies). Closes Tier 2 alongside SC and RA.
title: System and Services Acquisition Plan
description: Documents how the system is acquired, developed, documented, engineered, and maintained across the SDLC. Covers resource allocation, acquisition contract language, security-engineering principles, external system services, developer configuration management, developer testing, development process / tooling / standards, system documentation, and the lifecycle treatment of unsupported components. Covers the controls of the SA family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-160 v1 r1 (Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems), NIST SP 800-218 (Secure Software Development Framework — SSDF), NIST SP 800-64 r2 (SDLC integration — withdrawn but historically informative), NIST SP 800-161 r1 (SCRM), EO 14028, and OMB M-22-18.
intro_template:
This System and Services Acquisition Plan documents the acquisition, development, engineering, and lifecycle approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, tooling, cadences, and roles used to plan resources for security, integrate security into the SDLC, write security requirements into acquisition vehicles, evaluate external service providers, govern developer configuration management and testing, apply secure-engineering principles, maintain authoritative system documentation, and manage components reaching end of vendor support.

The scope covers SA-2 resource allocation, SA-3 SDLC integration, SA-4 acquisition, SA-5 documentation, SA-8 secure-engineering principles, SA-9 external system services, SA-10 developer configuration management, SA-11 developer testing, SA-15 secure development process / tooling, and SA-22 unsupported components within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (System and Services Acquisition family), NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF), NIST SP 800-160 v1 r1 (Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems), and NIST SP 800-161 r1 (SCRM).
approach_template:
{system_name} follows {sdlc_framework} as its system development life cycle, integrating security activities at every phase. Acquisition vehicles include {acquisition_vehicles}; security requirements in solicitations are derived from {requirements_source}. External system services in scope are evaluated under {external_service_framework}. Developer configuration management uses {dev_cm_tool}; developer testing is performed by {dev_test_tooling}.

Additional details on resource allocation, SDLC integration, acquisition requirements, system documentation, secure-engineering principles, external services, developer configuration management, developer testing, secure-development process, and unsupported-component lifecycle are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Acquisition-and-development performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (security-requirement coverage in solicitations, SBOM completeness rate, SAST / DAST / IAST findings closed within SLA, external-service authorization currency, unsupported-component count + remediation SLA, developer-CM adherence rate). The acquisition pipeline is reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; vendor end-of-life notices are monitored continuously and trigger SA-22 lifecycle actions before unsupported state is reached.
integration_template: This System and Services Acquisition Plan does not stand alone. The CM family inherits SA-10 developer configuration management as upstream of CM-2 / CM-3; the RA family consumes SA-11 testing outputs into RA-5 vulnerability data and revisits SA-15(3) criticality; the SR family extends SA-4 / SA-9 / SA-15(3) into formal supply-chain risk-management; the SI family verifies the integrity of artifacts produced by SA-15 secure tooling (SBOMs, signed packages); the AT family delivers SA-3-mandated developer / acquisition-staff training. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where SA-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Organizational contract language repository (FAR / DFARS clauses, security requirements)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Frameworks, vehicles, and tooling that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: SDLC framework (one-liner)
questions.help: SDLC methodology in use (e.g., 'DevSecOps with NIST SSDF integration', 'Agile (Scrum) + SSDF', 'Waterfall with security gates at each phase').

questions.label: Acquisition vehicles
questions.help: Primary contract vehicles (e.g., 'GSA Schedule 70 + GWAC + agency-specific BPA', 'Open-market FAR Part 12 commercial-item acquisitions', 'CRADAs with academic partners').

questions.label: Security-requirements source
questions.help: Where contract security requirements originate (e.g., 'Org standard contract language at /contracts/security-clauses.md derived from FAR 52.204-21 + DFARS 252.204-7012 + NIST 800-171').

questions.label: External-service evaluation framework
questions.help: How external services are vetted (e.g., 'FedRAMP authorization required for cloud services; SOC 2 Type II for non-FedRAMP SaaS; org SCRM review for partner integrations').

questions.label: Developer CM tool (one-liner)
questions.help: Repository / pipeline tooling (e.g., 'GitHub Enterprise + GitHub Actions; protected main branch; signed commits required'). Reference the CM Plan for system-side CM.

questions.label: Developer testing tooling
questions.help: SAST / DAST / SCA / IAST tools (e.g., 'GitHub CodeQL (SAST) + OWASP ZAP (DAST) + Snyk (SCA); Burp Suite for manual review').

family_questions.label: Resource Allocation (SA-2)
family_questions.description: Security funding and staffing in capital planning.

questions.label: Capital-planning integration
questions.help: How security resource needs are captured in capital planning (Exhibit 53 / 300 for federal). Investment-class line items, justification, multi-year planning.

questions.label: Security staffing model
questions.help: Roles + FTE allocation for security on this system (System Owner, ISSO, ISSM, security engineer, dev-security liaison, etc.).

questions.label: Budget-review cadence
questions.help: How often security budget is reviewed against actuals (typically tied to org budget cycle, e.g., 'Quarterly').

questions.label: Unfunded-requirements register
questions.help: Where unfunded security requirements are tracked (so they don't get lost). Often surfaces in the POA&M as risks pending funding.

family_questions.label: SDLC Integration (SA-3)
family_questions.description: Where in the SDLC security activities are integrated.

questions.label: Security activities by phase
questions.help: What security activity happens at each phase. Initiation: categorization + risk assessment. Development: threat modeling, secure coding, testing. Deployment: ATO. Operations: continuous monitoring. Disposal: sanitization + records retention.

questions.label: Threat-modeling approach
options: STRIDE per design / per architecture-significant change

questions.label: Developer-security training cadence
questions.help: Required training cadence for developers (e.g., 'Annual secure-coding training with role-based modules'). Reference AT plan if authored.

questions.label: SDLC-governance role
questions.help: Role accountable for SDLC-security adherence (e.g., 'Application Security Lead', 'CISO delegate').

family_questions.label: Acquisition Requirements (SA-4)
family_questions.description: Security clauses and deliverables required in contracts.

questions.label: Required security clauses
options: FAR 52.204-21 — Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information
DFARS 252.204-7012 — Safeguarding CDI / Cyber Incident Reporting
Section 889 — Prohibition on Certain Telecommunications Equipment

questions.label: Required security deliverables
options: SBOM in CycloneDX or SPDX format (SA-4(10))

questions.label: Continuous-monitoring contract clause (SA-4(7))
questions.help: How ongoing monitoring is required of vendors. ConMon deliverables, security-event reporting, vulnerability-disclosure obligations.

questions.label: SBOM acceptance criteria (SA-4(10))
questions.help: What an acceptable SBOM looks like (format, depth — direct vs transitive, machine-readable, signing). Reference EO 14028 / OMB M-22-18.

questions.label: Section 889 attestation evidence
questions.help: How vendor compliance with Section 889 (no Huawei / ZTE / Hikvision / Dahua / Hytera covered telecom) is collected and recorded.

family_questions.label: System Documentation (SA-5)
family_questions.description: Admin docs, user docs, and architecture documentation.

questions.label: Documentation storage location
questions.help: Authoritative location for system documentation (e.g., 'Confluence space CTLS at /docs.acme/CTLS', '/repo/docs in version control').

questions.label: Documentation currency-review cadence
questions.help: How often documentation is reviewed for currency (e.g., 'Annual + on significant change to architecture / configuration').

questions.label: Principles applied
options: Open design — no security through obscurity (SA-8(9))

questions.label: Evidence of application
questions.help: How application of these principles is evidenced (e.g., 'Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in /repo/adr cite which principle each decision aligns with'; 'Threat model captures principle-violation findings').

questions.label: Architecture-review role
questions.help: Role accountable for security-architecture review (e.g., 'Application Security Lead'; 'Security Architecture Review Board').

questions.label: External-service inventory location
questions.help: Where the inventory of external services in scope is maintained (CMDB section, dedicated SaaS-management tool, /repo/external-services.md).

questions.label: Authorization types accepted
options: DoD Cloud Computing SRG IL2 / IL4 / IL5 / IL6

questions.label: Data-flow documentation requirement
questions.help: How data flows between the system and each external service are documented (data classification labels exchanged, encryption-in-transit requirements, retention obligations).

questions.label: Authorization-currency tracking
questions.help: How authorization status is tracked through expiration (FedRAMP ATO sunset, SOC 2 report annual cadence). Renewal tickler process.

questions.label: Identification of functions / ports / protocols (SA-9(2))
questions.help: Per SA-9(2), the org identifies external service functions, ports, protocols, and other services for each external service in use.

questions.label: Service-termination procedure
questions.help: What happens when an external service contract ends (data return, sanitization attestation per MP / SC-28).

family_questions.label: Developer Configuration Management (SA-10)
family_questions.description: How developer-side configuration management is governed.

questions.label: Repository protections
options: Required PR review (≥2 approvers for security-sensitive paths)

questions.label: Developer-change classification
questions.help: How developer changes are classified (security-sensitive, normal, hotfix). Mapping to system-side CM-3 change classes.

questions.label: Release process
questions.help: From merge → release. Tagged releases, build artifacts, signing, deployment promotion through environments. Reference SI-7 for code authentication.

questions.label: Developer-baseline tracking (SA-10(1))
questions.help: How developer-side baselines (build configurations, dependency lockfiles, container base images) are tracked. Reference CM-2 system-side baselines.

questions.label: Integrity protection of build pipeline (SA-10(5))
questions.help: How the build pipeline itself is protected (RBAC on CI, secrets management, ephemeral runners, attestation per SLSA).

family_questions.label: Developer Testing and Evaluation (SA-11)
family_questions.description: SAST, DAST, SCA, IAST, fuzzing, code review.

questions.label: Testing types
options: Threat modeling and vulnerability analyses — SA-11(2)

questions.label: Testing cadence by type
questions.help: How often each test type runs. Example: 'SAST + SCA on every PR; DAST nightly against staging; fuzz-testing of parsing libraries weekly; manual pen-test annually + on significant change'.

questions.label: Finding-severity SLAs
questions.help: How developer-test findings are triaged. Severity-to-fix-time mapping (e.g., 'Critical SAST: blocks merge; High SAST: 7 days; Medium: next sprint').

questions.label: Results distribution
questions.help: Where developer-test results are recorded and who reviews them. Trends, regressions, exceptions.

questions.label: Independent review (SA-11(3))
questions.help: Per SA-11(3), independent verification of developer-test results. By a separate team within the org or by an external assessor.

family_questions.label: Secure Development Process / Standards / Tools (SA-15)
family_questions.description: The development process itself, the tooling chain, and standards.

questions.label: Secure-development tooling chain
questions.help: End-to-end tooling: IDE security plugins, version control with branch protection, CI with security gates, artifact signing, attestation generation. Reference SLSA levels if used.

questions.label: Secure coding standards followed
options: CERT Secure Coding Standards (C / C++ / Java)

questions.label: Criticality analysis in development (SA-15(3))
questions.help: Per SA-15(3), criticality analysis applied during development. Reference RA-9 for system-level. SBOM-based dependency criticality, mission-essential-function tracing.

questions.label: Developer screening (SA-15(8))
options: All developers in scope of org background investigation (typical for federal)
Vendor staff screened per contract clause

family_questions.label: Unsupported System Components (SA-22)
family_questions.description: Components past vendor support — replacement, alternative-source, or compensating control.

questions.label: Unsupported-component inventory location
questions.help: Where unsupported components are tracked (CMDB flag, dedicated EOL register). Linked to vendor product life-cycle calendars.

questions.label: Allowed remediation paths
options: Source alternative support from third party
Apply compensating controls (isolate + monitor) with formal risk acceptance

questions.label: Pre-EOL lead time target
questions.help: Time before vendor EOL by which remediation should be planned (e.g., '12 months').

questions.label: Compensating-controls inventory if isolation chosen
questions.help: Examples: network isolation, restricted access, increased monitoring, virtual patching via WAF / IPS rules. Reference RA-7 risk acceptance for the formal decision record.

family_questions.label: Acquisition / Development Scope
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: External services in scope
questions.help: Approximate count of external system services (cloud, SaaS, partner) in scope of SA-9.

questions.label: Active acquisition vehicles
questions.help: Approximate count of active acquisition vehicles supporting the system.

questions.label: Developers in scope of SA-3 / SA-11
questions.help: Approximate count of in-scope developers (gov, contractor, vendor staff).

questions.label: Unsupported / approaching-EOL components
questions.help: Current count of unsupported or pre-EOL components in the SA-22 register.

family_questions.label: Acquisition / Development Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate SA control effectiveness.

suggestions: % Developers current on annual security training
External-service authorization currency rate (% with valid auth)

questions.help: How often external-service authorization status is checked (FedRAMP marketplace, SOC 2 receipt, ISO certificate currency).

questions.label: Action on lapsed authorization
questions.help: What happens when an external service falls out of authorization (immediate suspension, grace-period processing, alternate-service fallback).

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the SA control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.12').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for SA findings
questions.help: Convention for SA-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-SA-' for general; 'POAM-SA22-' for unsupported-component-specific).

questions.label: CM family handoff
questions.help: How SA-10 developer CM feeds CM-2 system baselines and CM-3 change control. Where the handoff line sits (build → release → deploy).

questions.help: How SA-11 testing outputs feed RA-5 vulnerability data. SA-15(3) criticality echo with RA-9 system-level criticality.

glossary.definition: A contract, ordering agreement, or purchase mechanism through which goods or services are acquired (e.g., GSA Schedule, GWAC, BPA, single-award contract).
Architecture Decision Record — a short document capturing an architecture-significant decision, its context, and consequences. Common evidence vehicle for SA-8 principle application.
The set of points at which an unauthorized actor can attempt to interact with the system. Per SA-11(6), attack-surface reviews identify and reduce these points.
Business Associate Agreement — a HIPAA-required contract between a covered entity and a business associate handling PHI.
Defenders / attackers / collaborative-improvement teams. Purple team combines red and blue to drive defense improvement.
Blanket Purchase Agreement — a federal procurement vehicle for repetitive needs from a single vendor.
Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification — DoD framework assessing contractor cybersecurity posture against NIST SP 800-171.
Per SA-4(7), the practice of vendors continuously monitoring and reporting on their security posture during contract execution.
Dynamic Application Security Testing — runtime testing of a deployed application by sending crafted inputs and observing behavior.
The point at which a vendor will no longer issue security updates, bug fixes, or technical support for a product. Triggers SA-22 lifecycle action.
Federal Acquisition Regulation — the primary regulation for federal-government procurement.
Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program — the federal program for assessing and authorizing cloud services.
General Services Administration multiple-award schedules — a contract vehicle for federal agencies to acquire IT goods and services.
Government-Wide Acquisition Contract — a federal contract vehicle administered by a single agency for use by all federal agencies.
Interactive Application Security Testing — security testing performed inside a running application via instrumentation, combining SAST and DAST signals.

in-toto is a framework for software-supply-chain integrity attestations; SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) is a maturity model that uses such attestations. Common evidence for SA-10(5).
International Traffic in Arms Regulations / Export Administration Regulations — US export-control frameworks affecting acquisition of certain items.
Authorized simulated attack against a system to evaluate security. Per SA-11(5).
Privacy Impact Assessment — analysis of how PII is collected, used, shared, and disposed of. Required by RA-8 for systems handling PII.
Static Application Security Testing — analysis of source or compiled code without executing it. Per SA-11(1).
Software Bill of Materials — a formal record of components and dependencies in a piece of software. Required by SA-4(10) per EO 14028 / OMB M-22-18.
Software Composition Analysis — examining third-party components for known vulnerabilities and license compliance.
Supply Chain Risk Management — the practice of identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks in the supply chain. Driven by RA-3(1) and the SR family.
System Development Life Cycle — the phases through which a system passes from initiation to disposal. Subject to SA-3 security integration.
Section of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 requiring federal agencies to make their IT accessible to people with disabilities.
Section of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act prohibiting use of certain Chinese telecom and surveillance equipment in federal acquisition.
Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts — a security framework specifying levels of supply-chain integrity guarantees.
Service Organization Controls audit attesting to operating effectiveness of controls over a period (typically 6+ months). Common SaaS-vendor authorization vehicle.
Secure Software Development Framework — NIST SP 800-218, which establishes practices for integrating security into the SDLC. Mandated by EO 14028 for federal-system suppliers.
The structured process of identifying threats, vulnerabilities, and countermeasures during system design. Per SA-11(2) and SA-15(4).
A system component that no longer receives vendor security updates. Subject to SA-22 lifecycle treatment.
